rows.description: A young adult holds a losing stock or a failing project too long to avoid the pain of realising the loss, while selling winners too soon.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague notices that people fight harder to keep a benefit than to gain an equal one. He frames proposals to show what is protected, and admits honestly what is given up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A thoughtful person imagines a loss and a gain of the same size and asks which she would truly prefer, easing the automatic tilt toward the safe option.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young child treats a toy as far more precious once it is his and refuses a fair swap. Ownership alone raises its value in his mind.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child demands more than a card is worth because it is his own, and thinks others are cheating when they will not pay. Buyers and owners rarely agree on value.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student refuses to sell an old bike or drop a first draft because it is his, valuing it above the market or above a better alternative.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A flatmate sees a seller price his used phone far above what buyers offer. A useful check is asking whether he would pay that price to buy it today.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A child insists on the same seat, same breakfast and same route even when alternatives are fine. Change feels riskier than continuing what he knows.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager drifts into the stream everyone in the family chose, because switching feels effortful and risky. The default becomes a decision he never actually made.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult stays with an overpriced plan, a weak course or a weak habit only because changing needs effort. Inertia hides as contentment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
